# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 96 (Bi-Vb Pc96)
**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc96
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 96
**Title (English, from literature):** Not wearing a chest wrap
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bi-vb-pc96

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 96 (*Saṁkakṣikā*) is an expiation rule for Buddhist nuns concerning the wearing of a chest wrap or bust cover (*saṁkacchika*) [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. The rule stipulates that a nun who enters an inhabited village or area without wearing a bust cover commits an offense that must be confessed [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. According to its background story (*nidāna*), the regulation was laid down after a nun entered a settlement without a chest wrap; when a whirlwind blew her upper robe aside in the street, onlookers praised her waist, causing her acute embarrassment [Hüsken 1997]. The word analysis and commentary (such as the *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī*) define the garment as covering the torso below the collarbone and above the navel, while the exemption formula (*anāpatti*) conforms to the standard exemptions found in monastic robe regulations [Hüsken 1997].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include the rule in the Pali Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Bhikkhunī Parivāra (Pc 96), as well as corresponding rules across other early Vinaya traditions: Dharmaguptaka (Bi Vb Pc 160), Mahīśāsaka (Bi Vb Pc 181), Mahāsāṅghika (Bi Vb Pc 74), and the Sanskrit Lokottaravāda Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Pc 74) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus aligns segments of the text with a Sanskrit *Prātimokṣasūtra* and identifies extensive shared phrasing across the Pali Vinaya, including Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 3, numerous other Pācittiya rules (such as Pc 15, Pc 25, Pc 48, Pc 55, and Pc 86), and sub-commentarial works like the *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇīpurāṇa-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
